# Completed lane claims — archive

Rows moved out of [`LANES.md`](LANES.md) once their status became terminal
(`done`, `released`, `yielded`, `retracted`, `withdrawn`, `superseded`,
`closed`, `resolved`). **Nothing is lost** — this is a relocation, and every row
is reproduced verbatim, in its original order.

**Why:** `LANES.md` had grown to 661 KB across 213 rows, and 170 of those were
finished work. It is the file every agent is told to read before starting, so
its size is a direct cost on every session, and a finished row competes for
attention with a live one. Coordination needs the *live* board; the record needs
to survive. This file is the record.

**Read this file when** you want the reasoning behind a completed lane: what was
measured, what was tried and abandoned, and the warnings terminal rows carry
(`do not re-post`, `do not retry`, `RETRACTED — scoped on a false premise`).
Several of these are the only written account of why an approach does not work.

**Do not claim from this file.** Live lanes are in `LANES.md`; a row here is
history. If a completed row describes work you believe is not actually done,
post a *new* row in `LANES.md` with the evidence rather than reviving this one.

| edward (fable) | `DavisKahan/Experimental/InfiniteDimensional/Ideals/Symmetric.lean` — **one new theorem plus a norm helper; no existing statement, proof or name changed.** **Does NOT touch** any other module, `comparator/*.json`, or `Challenge/**`. | **`SymmetricNormIdeal` has unitary invariance only in the *conjugation* form, and the two-sided form is what every singular-value argument actually needs.** The structure field `unitary_invariant` and its wrapper `gauge_unitary_conjugation` both give `gauge (U A U⁻¹) = gauge A`. But two operators with the same singular values are related by `A = U B V` with **two independent** unitaries, not by conjugation — so the conjugation form does not apply, and there is currently no route from "same singular values" to "same gauge" for an abstract symmetric ideal. **Found while looking at a leaf obligation it blocks.** `SymmetricNormIdeal.sinAngle_reflected_mem_gauge_eq` (`InfiniteDimensional/DoubleAngle.lean:598`) is a bare `sorry` whose own docstring gives the intended proof — *"their singular values agree"* — and that proof cannot be written today, because the step it needs does not exist. For (3), `A ∘ₗ A⁺ = ∑ᵢ (σᵢ²)⁻¹ • rankOne (A vᵢ) (A vᵢ)`, self-adjoint because `adjoint (rankOne x y) = rankOne y x` and the coefficients are real. Uniqueness is the standard four-identity argument.
